text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli soldier killed, three others wounded in Hizbollah attack. Comment: Alternatives to security zone in Lebanon provide worse scenarios.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton: Clear Hebron hurdle. Member of parliament claims Kiryat Arba settler stoned him.
- Iran said willing to help find missing Israeli navigator Ron Arad.
- Ultra-Orthodox Jews attack car near Bar-Ilan Street in Jerusalem on sabbath.
- Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara: Israel-Syria talks won't resume until 1997.
HAARETZ
- Syrian foreign minister expects: Peace talks will apparently resume at the start of 1997.
- Clinton: The first issue the new administration will deal with will be the redeployment in Hebron.
- Comment: A change in Israeli-Iranian relations. Tehran's promise to help in locating navigator Ron Arad: "We're speaking of a humanitarian issue."
- Commission to examine Israeli army motivation: "There has been no drop in motivation among right-wing youth".
MAARIV
- Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani: We'll arrest 30 extremist Jews ahead of Hebron evacuation. Target date: November 20-22.
- Given tensions surrounding Hebron, question is will Netanyahu go to the United States?
- New York Times report on how Hizbollah intended to carry out terror attacks in the heart of Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israeli army cancels closure nearly entirely this morning.
- U.S. effort to complete Hebron agreement this week.
